learning_outcomes.text: Know how a radio transceiver is constructed.
Understand how the practical receiver differs from the theoretical models.
Know how to model a non-ideal transceiver and how to measure the errors produced by the non-ideal behavior of the transceiver.
Understand the structure of a software project.
Be able to participate in a large software project with multiple programmers.
Know the basics of problem solving methods.
Be able to apply problem solving methods in your own projects.
Predict how the interference impacts radio links and radio communication systems in general.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory works using software radios (universal software radio platform (USRP) and GNU-radio framework)
Description and measurement of radio performance
Structuring a software project using GNU-radio as an example
Creating and adding new functions to the software based transceiver chain
